content.value_statement: Live meeting work often needs current events, clear identity routing, and careful write actions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Lark CLI meeting join, events, messages, active meeting lookup, and leave workflows.
actual_capabilities: Join an active Lark meeting as an application bot by 9-digit meeting number.
List active meetings visible to a user or bot identity.
Read current meeting events with pagination guidance.
Send in-meeting text messages or approved reaction emoji.
Leave a meeting when the user explicitly requests bot departure.
Route ended meeting, transcript, recording, and IM tasks to related Lark skills.
limitations: It requires lark-cli, valid Lark authentication, and tenant permissions.
It does not search ended meetings, transcripts, recordings, or participant snapshots.
Bot join, message, reaction, and leave actions are visible to meeting participants.
Access depends on tenant installation, data scope, scopes, and beta availability.

use_cases.title: Monitor a Live Meeting
use_cases.description: Find the active meeting, refresh visible events, and summarize recent speakers, chat, and sharing.

use_cases.title: Operate a Bot Attendee
use_cases.description: Join a meeting as the application bot, capture the meeting ID, and leave only on request.

use_cases.title: Send In-Meeting Feedback
use_cases.description: Send a text prompt or approved reaction emoji using the same identity that found the meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Find My Current Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lark-vc-agent to find my current active Lark meeting and show the meeting_id candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Read Live Meeting Events
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate event review for a known meeting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current meeting_id to read all visible live meeting events with the same identity. Summarize recent speakers, chats, and sharing.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Meeting Reaction
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate write action with identity continuity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the active meeting by this 9-digit meeting number, then send a thumbs-up reaction if exactly one active match is found.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Bot Attendance
prompt_templates.prompt: Join meeting 123456789 as the bot, capture the returned meeting_id, poll visible events, and leave only if I explicitly ask.

output_examples.input: What is happening in my current meeting?
output_examples.output: I found one active meeting, refreshed the event stream, and summarized the current speakers, chat messages, and shared content.

output_examples.input: Send a thumbs-up in this meeting.
output_examples.output: I matched the active meeting, kept the same identity, and sent the approved thumbs-up reaction.

output_examples.input: Make the bot join this meeting and follow the discussion.
output_examples.output: The bot joined the meeting, saved the returned meeting ID, and used it to read visible live events.

best_practices: Confirm the meeting number, meeting ID, and identity before any visible write action.
Use full pagination when summarizing current meeting events.
Use dry-run previews when the target meeting or identity is uncertain.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every 9-digit meeting number as permission to join.
Do not switch identities after discovering a meeting ID.
Do not use live event reads for ended meeting transcripts or recordings.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides Lark CLI workflows for live meeting actions, event reads, messages, reactions, active meeting lookup, and bot leave.

faq.question: Does it join meetings automatically?
faq.answer: No. It should join only when the user clearly asks for the bot to enter a live meeting.

faq.question: Can it read ended meeting transcripts?
faq.answer: No. Ended meetings, transcripts, recordings, and participant snapshots belong to related Lark meeting skills.

faq.question: Which identity should it use?
faq.answer: It keeps the same user or bot identity that discovered the meeting ID.

faq.question: Can it send meeting messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can send text or approved reaction emoji when permissions and meeting state allow it.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: It depends on Lark tenant installation, scopes, data range settings, authentication, and beta access.
